checked.claim: EUR 50m in Jan 2019; CE rejected appeal 19 June 2020 (430810); CNIL competent as Google had no EU main establishment
checked.evidence: CE 430810, 19 June 2020: appeal rejected; fine imposed by deliberation SAN-2019-001 of 21 January 2019; Google Ireland had 'no decision-making power' over the processing, so Google LLC had no main establishment in the EU.
CNIL decision 21 Jan 2019, CE decision 19 June 2020.

checked.claim: 3 Sept 2025, Google EUR 325m and Shein EUR 150m for trackers without consent, cookie walls and Gmail ads, under Art. 82 LIL
checked.evidence: CNIL 3 Sept 2025: Google EUR 325m, Shein EUR 150m. Shein: Art. 82 only (trackers without consent). Google: Art. 82 for cookies at account creation (consent not freely given) and Art. L. 34-5 CPCE for ads in Gmail's Promotions and Social tabs without prior consent. The summary wrongly put the Gmail ads under Art. 82 and attributed all breaches to both companies.
checked.replacement: On 3 September 2025 the CNIL fined Google EUR 325 million and Shein EUR 150 million. Both were sanctioned under Art. 82 Loi Informatique et Libertés for cookie consent failures; Google was also sanctioned under Art. L. 34-5 of the Postal and Electronic Communications Code for showing ads in Gmail without prior consent. Appeal status not confirmed.

checked.evidence: CNIL simplified procedure page: EUR 20,000 / EUR 100 per day, and EUR 100,000 / EUR 500 per day for turnover above EUR 50 million; confirmed by a September 2026 law firm note. checked.claim: Conseil d'État, first and last instance, full jurisdiction
checked.evidence: CE decided Google LLC directly; law firm note: the judge 'may annul or reform the decision', reducing fines.

CNIL: two months from notification of the deliberation. Law firm note: extended to four months for entities abroad (the two-month extension under Art. R. 421-7 Code de justice administrative). Readers outside France would act on the wrong deadline.
checked.replacement: Two months from notification of the decision, extended by two months for organisations established outside France (Art. R. 421-7 Code de justice administrative).

checked.claim: Not suspensive; référé-suspension possible; provision not confirmed
checked.evidence: Law firm note: the appeal does not suspend the decision and the periodic penalty runs from the date fixed; suspension under Art. L. 521-1 CJA requires urgency and serious doubt as to legality. Secondary source only.
checked.replacement: Not suspensive: the decision and any periodic penalty apply despite the appeal. The organisation can ask the Conseil d'État's interim relief judge for suspension (référé-suspension, Art. L. 521-1 Code de justice administrative), which requires urgency and serious doubt as to legality.
